plain: To bring about or carry out.

webster.text: To bring to pass; to achieve; to accomplish; to fulfil; as, to effectuate a purpose or desire.

example.quote: I say, ivill be amended, because the Constitution is constructed on such principles, that its bad effects, if any such should arise from it, will injure the members of Congress equally with their constituents; and, tlierefore, both of them must be equally induced to seek for, and effectuate, if possible, the requisite amendments.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Massachusetts Convention, Hon. Mr. BOWDOIN, January 23, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
